True Prudhvi. That's a good enough workaround. But like every workaround has
its own problems and limitations, this too has some.  F-score is already a
aggregation (harmonic mean) of precision and recall. If we have 20 classes, by
'overall f-score' we are actually adding another layer of aggregation on top
it.  This might have following issues:  1\. Every such aggregation suffers
from domination of larger values.2. As the aggregation layer increases, we
keep loosing interpretation. On the other hand, Kappa statistic takes care of
this inherently.In addition to it, Kappa also compares the observed accuracy
with the expected accuracy. For example, 90% accuracy is really good when
expected accuracy is 50% but it is not impressive when expected accuracy is
itself 80% which is generally the case with imbalanced datasets. In a
nutshell, Kappa is a right measure to use when we have multi-class
classification over imbalanced datasets. (edited)
